Town water works: reference notes.

Intake and storage
- raw water is drawn from the upland reservoir through two intake pipes at the north dam
- each intake pipe carries up to four million litres of water per day to the pumping station
- the reservoir holds about ninety days of supply when it is full in early spring
- a screen at each intake keeps leaves, fish and floating debris out of the pipes
- the station keeps one intake pipe in reserve while the other is cleaned every autumn
- reservoir levels are read each morning and posted on the board in the station office
Notes checked at the spring review.

Treatment hall
- raw water first passes through a mixing tank where a coagulant gathers fine particles together
- settled water then flows through six sand filters that remove most of the remaining sediment
- the sand filters are backwashed with clean water once every two days to clear trapped silt
- chlorine is dosed after filtration so that the treated water stays safe in the town mains
- operators test the chlorine level in the treated water every four hours during each shift
- every chlorine reading is written into the daily log kept on the desk in the treatment hall
- a second operator signs the daily log at the end of each shift before handing over
Notes checked at the spring review.

Storage and distribution
- treated water is pumped uphill to a covered service tank above the old market square
- the service tank holds enough treated water to supply the whole town for about one day
- gravity carries water from the service tank down through the mains to every street
- the oldest cast iron mains under the market square are being replaced with plastic pipe
- a leak survey of the town mains is carried out by night when demand is at its lowest
- burst mains are repaired by a standby crew that can reach any street within one hour
Notes checked at the spring review.

Staffing and records
- the water works employs eleven people across three shifts and one office day shift
- new operators train for six weeks alongside a senior operator before working alone
- monthly water quality reports are sent to the town council and pinned in the library
- pump running hours are logged weekly so that motors are serviced before they wear out
- the station keeps a spare pump motor in the store room beside the workshop door
Notes checked at the spring review.
